**`(*renderer).addArg` — `internal/filter/render.go:842` — ~28 call sites (14 distinct calling functions).**

`addArg` is the SQL-parameter accumulator for the filter engine: every literal that ends up in a generated `WHERE` clause is passed through it to get a dialect-appropriate placeholder and be appended to the args slice. That makes it the single most-called symbol declared anywhere under `internal/`.

All 28 call sites are inside `internal/filter/render.go` itself, spread across 14 methods. The heaviest users are `renderTagInList` (6 calls, since it builds exact- and prefix-match pairs per dialect at lines 454-467), `renderElementInCondition` (3), and `foldedLike` (3), with the rest — `renderTagStartsWith`, `renderScalarInCondition`, `renderScalarComparison`, `renderRegex`, `buildJSONArrayLike`, `renderTagEquals`, `renderJSONBoolComparison`, `renderFunctionComparison`, `renderAccessorComparison`, `elementPredicateSQL`, and `addBoolArg` — contributing one or two each.

How I ranked it. I enumerated every function and method declared under `internal/` and counted non-declaration call sites in non-generated, non-test Go files, then manually filtered false positives. The runners-up, all also in the filter package, were `Schema.Field` (`internal/filter/schema.go:67`) at 19 call sites across `parser.go` and `render.go`, `jsonArrayExpr` at 16, `renderChildren` at 14, and `getConstValue` at 13.

Two names scored higher in the raw grep but are not real: `.Next(` at 55 is almost entirely `rows.Next()` from `database/sql` — `Schedule.Next` (`internal/scheduler/parser.go:92`) has exactly one caller, at `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:142` — and `New` at 236 is dominated by constructors in other packages and the standard library.

For contrast, the most-called *exported* symbols in `internal/` are far lower: `util.GenUUID` (`internal/util/util.go:40`) at 7 callers, `filter.DefaultEngine` (`internal/filter/engine.go:111`) at 7, `Engine.CompileToStatement` (`internal/filter/engine.go:74`) at 7, and `filter.AppendConditions` (`internal/filter/helpers.go:9`) at 6. So if you specifically want the highest fan-in across *package boundaries* rather than overall, it's a three-way tie around 7; `addArg` wins outright on total inbound calls.
